title: Expenses by Function & Nature
description: Classify program services and supporting services and understand expense reporting by function and nature.
html:
Why NFP Expense Reporting Is Different

Not-for-profit organizations report expenses in a way that helps users understand both:

FUNCTION = WHY THE COST WAS INCURRED NATURE = WHAT TYPE OF COST IT WAS

Functional Classification

Functional classification groups expenses according to the purpose they serve.

Program Services Activities That Directly Carry Out the NFP's Mission
Management & General Administrative and Overall Support Activities
Fundraising Activities Designed to Obtain Contributions

Program Services

Program services are activities that directly accomplish the organization's mission.

Example

A food-assistance charity pays employees who distribute meals directly to families.

Those salary costs are generally classified functionally as program service expense.

Management & General

Management and general expenses support the overall administration and operation of the NFP rather than one specific program.

Examples

  • General accounting
  • Executive administration
  • Human resources
  • General legal services

Fundraising

Fundraising expenses are costs incurred to encourage donors to contribute resources to the organization.

Example

An NFP pays $15,000 to organize a donor solicitation campaign.

That amount is generally classified as a fundraising expense.

Natural Classification

Natural classification describes the economic type of expense.

Salaries Natural Classification
Rent Natural Classification
Utilities Natural Classification
Depreciation Natural Classification
Supplies Natural Classification

One Expense Can Have Both

The same cost can be classified by both its nature and its function.

Example

An employee earns $50,000 working entirely in an educational program.

Nature Salaries
Function Program Services

Allocating Shared Costs

Some expenses benefit more than one function. In that case, the organization generally allocates the costs using a reasonable and appropriate method.

Example

A building is used:

  • 70% for program services
  • 20% for management and general
  • 10% for fundraising

Annual rent is $100,000.

Program = $70,000 Management & General = $20,000 Fundraising = $10,000

Supporting Services

Management and general and fundraising are commonly grouped as supporting services.

PROGRAM SERVICES ≠ SUPPORTING SERVICES SUPPORTING SERVICES GENERALLY INCLUDE: MANAGEMENT & GENERAL + FUNDRAISING

Why This Matters

Expense classification helps financial statement users evaluate how an NFP uses its resources.

For example, users may want to know how much spending goes directly toward mission-related programs versus administrative or fundraising activities.

Statement of Functional Expenses

An NFP must present information about expenses by both nature and function in one location.

This information may be presented in the financial statements, in the notes, or through a separate statement of functional expenses, depending on presentation.

CPA Classification Example

A health charity incurs:

Medical Staff Salaries $200,000
Accounting Staff Salaries $60,000
Fundraising Campaign Costs $40,000
FUNCTIONALLY: PROGRAM SERVICES = $200,000 MANAGEMENT & GENERAL = $60,000 FUNDRAISING = $40,000

From a natural classification perspective, the first two amounts are both salary expense, even though their functional classifications differ.

CPA Memory Rule

FUNCTION = PURPOSE NATURE = TYPE PROGRAM = MISSION MANAGEMENT + FUNDRAISING = SUPPORT

Key Takeaways

  • NFP expenses are analyzed by both function and nature.
  • Program services directly support the organization's mission.
  • Management and general and fundraising are supporting services.
  • Natural classifications describe the type of cost.
  • Shared costs should be allocated using a reasonable method.

quiz.prompt: An NFP pays $80,000 of salaries to employees who work directly in its primary charitable program. Which combination best describes this expense?

choices.text: Nature: Salaries; Function: Management and general

quiz.explanation: Salaries describe the natural classification, while program services describe the functional classification because the employees work directly on the NFP's mission-related program.
